Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- The FOMC’s July 27, 2022 statement remains hawkish: activity has softened while inflation is elevated; policy was tightened 75 bps to 2.25–2.50% with guidance for ongoing hikes and continued balance-sheet runoff (ramping in September).
- The July 2022 SLOOS points to a notable tightening in credit supply that reinforces growth headwinds from policy:
  - Banks tightened standards and terms for C&I loans across large, middle-market, and small firms; increased loan pricing and collateral requirements; and cited a weaker economic outlook, industry-specific issues, and liquidity as key reasons.
  - Standards tightened for commercial real estate and for residential real estate (including GSE-eligible and jumbo), as well as for consumer credit (credit cards, subprime auto) and HELOCs.
  - Demand signals were mixed: stronger demand for C&I (including from small firms) and HELOCs, but weaker demand across CRE categories.
- Implications: Broad-based tightening in lending standards and higher borrowing costs/requirements suggest the credit channel will transmit Fed tightening more forcefully, adding downside risk to growth and to credit-sensitive sectors (CRE, RRE, consumer). Stronger C&I and HELOC demand tempers this somewhat but may reflect precautionary draws. Net tone shifts slightly more negative versus a macro-only or FSR-tilted read.

Net tone: moderately negative, somewhat more cautious given tighter bank lending supply.
